images.title: Pond water
images.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: a close-up landscape concept sheet for Little Rome, derived from the supplied original town concept art.
Input images: these are style, palette, material and subject references. Recompose the existing landscape elements into a NEW detailed study; preserve their established art direction.
Style: the same premium handcrafted 3D miniature diorama as the references, with rich but restrained Mediterranean colour, softly sculpted natural forms, exceptionally fine tactile surfaces, warm limestone and ochre earth, layered sage/olive foliage, crisp small details, believable soft contact shadows and warm directional light. Keep the charming carefully made miniature quality and readable shapes. High-quality finished concept illustration, not a photograph of a real landscape and not an illustration in a different art style.
Composition: landscape format, generous resolution, the featured pieces occupy most of the sheet at a much larger scale than in the town images. Subtle muted blue-grey studio atmosphere and clean spacing, no visible frames or drawn diagrams. Show enough context to understand how the surfaces meet. Keep almost all featured detail in focus; use depth of field only in the far background.
Constraints: expand detail of the existing landscape vocabulary only. No people, buildings, temples, wells, vehicles, animals, statues or new gameplay objects. No UI, titles, labels, letters, arrows, border or watermark. No low-poly facets, flat paper foliage, plastic shine, cartoon outlines or unrelated fantasy elements.

Subject: the pond WATER from the town concepts, shown as one large three-quarter overhead close view occupying the upper two thirds, plus two smaller surface studies beneath it. Preserve the reference's irregular small garden pond, natural pale limestone banks, sparse reeds and scattered lily pads.
Main view: luminous clear turquoise-to-deep-teal water. Distinguish transparent warm shallow margins with visible submerged pebbles and softened stone silhouettes from deeper blue-green water. Soft, broken reflections of nearby cypress and olive foliage coexist with the sense of depth. Natural overlapping ripples of several scales, subtle sun glints, gentle contact shadows below lily pads, slight refraction at stems, and fine restrained caustics in the shallow sunlit water. The pond surface is the focus, not a whole landscape.
Lower studies: one much closer summer shallow-water patch where water laps a partly submerged limestone edge and lily pad; one wet winter surface patch in cool blue-grey light showing a few clear overlapping circular raindrop impact rings, reflected reeds and small water droplets. Show physical water, never a repeating zigzag distortion, opaque blue paint, thick glass slab or ocean waves. No snow or ice.

Subject: an intimate close-up of the pond's BANK, where irregular warm pale limestone, damp earth, fine pebbles, moss, reeds and lily pads meet the water. One large three-quarter study of a curved shoreline segment fills most of the image, accompanied by two smaller uncluttered detail studies at the bottom: a reed clump rooted through wet sediment, and several floating lily pads seen close enough to read their curled edges, vein structure and tiny droplets.
The bank must retain the original town concept's natural garden-pond character. Vary stone size, orientation and spacing; some stones sit partly submerged, with a dark damp waterline, ochre mineral speckling, tiny fractures and softened underwater edges. Clear shallows reveal gravel becoming darker and less visible with depth. Moss and small herb roots occur in sheltered crevices; reeds have individual tapering leaves and visible stems entering the water. Lily pads vary in age and green tone, some overlap naturally; their reflected edges and contact shadows are subtle. Warm spring light; turquoise water. Show surfaces and transitions as finely crafted miniature assets rather than a rigid circular retaining wall.

Subject: the two defining tree types already visible in the town references: a mature olive tree and a tall Mediterranean cypress. Present the complete olive tree on the left and complete cypress on the right at a clear comparable miniature scale, each grounded in a small irregular patch of soil, grasses and limestone. Include two close detail studies below: olive branch/leaf cluster with its junction to the textured trunk, and a cypress branch spray with its layered scale-like foliage.
Preserve the original olive's twisting branched trunk and open, asymmetric spreading crown; dense clusters of many narrow rounded silver-green leaves have warm green upper faces and muted pale undersides. Show real branching and pockets of air through the crown, not a ball or flat cloud. Trunk bark is subtly fissured and rooted into the ground. Cypress has an elegant tapered silhouette, a slightly irregular living outline, branching green sprays packed in layered depths and shaded inner foliage; never stacked cones, beads, or triangular cards. The root flare and connection to ground should be readable. Fine sculpted leaf geometry and restrained natural variation, warm sun with soft green bounce, the exact rich handcrafted miniature style of the original town.

Subject: detailed low Mediterranean planting already suggested around the town: fine meadow grasses, small branching aromatic herbs, low silvery-green shrubs, tiny white and yellow wildflowers, sparse pale-purple flowers and creeping groundcover. Create one cohesive landscape concept sheet with four separated, generous close-up planting patches arranged naturally: mixed grass and daisies; a woody branching herb with slender leaves and sparse pale-purple blooms; a small silvery shrub beside limestone; a blended mixed border of groundcover, grasses and scattered yellow flowers. The lower edge can include a few enlarged leaf/stem and soil-contact details without diagram symbols.
Each patch grows from a small irregular piece of earthy ground with roots, tiny pebbles, dry stems and open soil between clumps. Avoid one solid green carpet. Show varied grass blade length, bending, seed heads, branching structure, readable little flower petals, delicate leaf thickness, soft self-shadowing and occasional sunlit translucent edges. Keep plant mass and palette faithful to the rich spring/summer miniature references, with only a few warm dry stems and autumn leaves for restrained variation. These are close asset studies, not an entire meadow panorama.

Subject: a close asset study of one corner of the cube landscape from the original references: the meeting of the playable grassy top, dark ochre soil cap, roots, trailing small vines, and the exposed pale fractured limestone side. One large three-quarter corner study fills the left and centre; two smaller details on the right show an individual weathered limestone outcrop and the soil-to-rock-to-root transition at high magnification.
Preserve the cube's recognizable vertical side while making the rock natural: irregular interlocking fractured masses of varied scale, angular breaks softened by weathering, fine granular texture, subtle strata and mineral colour variation, deep but restrained crevice shadows, embedded little stones and occasional earth-filled cracks. Avoid uniform rectangular masonry, repeated identical rocks, exaggerated caves, holes through the cube, or a flat wall texture. Grass and low plants grow over an uneven top rim; the soil cap has fine grains, roots and a few exposed pebbles. Sparse olive-green trailing vines cling to sheltered fissures, with a few restrained ochre autumn leaves. Warm pale cream stone, rusty earth and natural greens, crisp rich miniature surfaces, same art direction as the town reference.

Subject: close-up landscape surfaces connecting the town: an irregular pale limestone footpath and its transition into grassy ground and a cultivated field edge. The main study is a detailed diagonal length of the path in warm summer light, with uneven hand-fitted polygonal paving stones, fine joints, worn edges, tiny chips, embedded grit, subtle height variation and occasional grass or herb growth in the margins. Along one side, show rich crumbly cultivated earth and a small section of the existing simple weathered wooden field fence, with a few leafy crop starts and sparse straw only as scale/context. The opposite edge blends naturally into fine grass, small herbs and scattered stones.
Below the main view, show two smaller surface studies of the same paving: dry stone with warm pores and worn corners; wet winter stone with darker saturated material, a thin irregular puddle bridging low joints, restrained reflected sky/foliage and tiny rain ripples. No snow or ice. Retain the reference's warm hand-crafted miniature quality and readable stone shapes; no uniform tiles, giant cracks, polished marble, glossy varnish or repeated identical paving units. Prioritize material transitions and field-border construction over buildings or scenery.
